topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Foundations of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immunity detects infection and damage through appropriately positioned receptors for distinctive molecular patterns.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how toll-like receptors translate microbial recognition into immune responses suited to the location of the detected threat.

topics.label: Non-TLR recognition and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how recognition pathways beyond toll-like receptors trigger inflammation that can contribute to disease.

topics.label: Sentinel-driven inflammation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated sentinel cells initiate inflammatory responses that bring circulating leukocytes to an infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how infection signals reach lymph nodes to initiate adaptive immune responses.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation becomes a life-threatening systemic response.

topics.label: Mechanisms of inflammation resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammatory activity is shut down through the balance of passive decay and active inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine tissue recovery after inflammation and why unresolved causes can require a persistent inflammatory response.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and identifies complement as the subject of the next session.
